## Summary

**STOREILM** (Store Inverted Long masked register into memory): Store 8 byte from register-b in memory when its mask=0.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `b → <vea> depending on mask.` |
| Syntax | `STOREILM b,mask,<vea>`<br>Where 8 lsb bits are used as mask to write (0) or not (1) |
| Short | Store 8 byte from register-b in memory when its mask=0 |
| Description | Store is a conditional write of 8 bytes. The selection is made by the lsb of the 8 bytes from register d. |
| Condition codes | not affected |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–9 | `1111111` |
| 1 | 8 | A |
| 1 | 7 | B |
| 1 | 6 | D |
| 1 | 5–3 | Mode |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |
| 2 | 15–12 | b |
| 2 | 11–8 | d (mask) |
| 2 | 7–0 | `00100101` |

- Not allowed &lt;vea&gt; : #imm
- No masking is done when destination is a register.

### Example

```asm
    storem    d0,d1,(a2)
```

```text
b d0: 11 22 33 44 55 66 77 88
d d1: 01 01 00 01 01 00 00 01
Result:
```

- vea (a2) memory content where a2 points to

```text
.. .. 33 .. .. 66 77 ..
```

### Notes

- Also called storem2
- Storem is similar

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no STOREILM. It is new on the 68080.

## Do / Don't

- DON'T use an immediate `<vea>`.
